inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 548.75m ordinary shares issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 6-K balance sheet, post the $400m H1-26 buyback) plus ~7m dilutive employee equity (Q2 2026 diluted 556m vs basic 549m weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.cash_note: Cash 1,087 + current marketable securities 1,270 + non-current marketable securities 946 = 3,303 at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 6-K). CashAndEquivalents in the Metrics CSV is cash-only and understates liquid resources by ~$2.2bn; the marketable securities are US Treasuries/GSEs/corporate debt (Level 1-2) held in the kpis table as MarketableSecurities. Total debt 1,122 = current 98 + non-current 1,024 long-term debt, EXCLUDING 556 of lease obligations (see lease_treatment).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' 200 (FY24 186, FY23 150). Equity-award tax withholding is immaterial: 'Proceeds from issuance of equity instruments' net of taxes was -5 in FY2025, so no separate add-on. Finance income 159 (FY2025 income statement) stripped because net cash of ~$2.2bn is >3x the owner-FCF base.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks were nil; H1 2026 repurchased $400m ($300m from Mubadala at $40.85 on 2026-03-13 plus $100m open market at $43.88 avg) under the $500m Feb-2026 authorisation, ~$100m remaining. First-ever quarterly dividend of $0.12/share paid July 2026; capital-return framework targets up to 50% of TTM non-IFRS adjusted FCF. Distributions are value-neutral in this model (the flat count is being funded), so no payout is assumed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10-year UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.2 x ERP ~5.0% = ~10.2% cost of equity; debt is ~4% of enterprise capital at ~5% pre-tax with little tax shield, so WACC rounds to 10.0%. No ad-hoc cyclicality or controlled-company premium is stacked on top: cyclicality is charged in the flows (mid-cycle margin path, an explicit down-cycle in the bear case, 25% bear weight) and the WACC is identical across scenarios so risk is charged exactly once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full lease cash payment (principal + interest; H1-26 cash outflow for leases $35m, H1-25 $56m, ~1.0-1.5% of revenue) is charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.2% of revenue, and the 556 of IFRS-16 lease obligations (61 current + 495 non-current at 2026-06-30) is EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for cash-tax EBIT excludes ~$50m/yr of right-of-use depreciation (FY25 total D&A 1,314 incl. ROU -> ~1,264 = 18.6% of revenue ex-ROU).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests of 56 (Q2 2026 balance sheet; NCI share of profit only 3 in FY2025) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are left consolidated because the NCI leakage is <0.5% of net income.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). GF is a specialty (non-leading-edge) semiconductor foundry with owned fabs: high fixed costs, shipment-utilisation-driven margins, revenue 8,108 at the FY2022 peak -> 6,750 at the FY2024 trough -> ~7,250 guided for FY2026. FY2024's -214 operating loss is entirely the $935m Q4-2024 impairment of legacy Malta NY capacity (FY2024 20-F, impairment note) on a positive 1,651 gross profit; pre-SBC EBITDA ex that charge was 2,475 (36.7%). The base is built MID-CYCLE: pre-SBC EBITDA margin 32.5% rising to 35% (history 36.6-36.9% FY22-24 at peak utilisation, 34.0% FY25, 32.2% H1-26 as the MIPS/ARC/AMF/InfiniLink acquisitions stepped up R&D opex while GM recovered to 28-30%); capex 19% of revenue falling to 16% net of CHIPS/NY State grant receipts (>$16bn gross over 10+ years, ~$1.6bn/yr gross, offset by $1.5bn CHIPS DFA + $570m NY State + 35% AMITC); cash tax ramped from ~4% to 15% over ten years given the $12.4bn accumulated deficit, unrecognised NOLs (+$743m from OBBBA R&D expensing) and the 35% AMITC. Working capital: manufacturer, receivables + inventory > payables, so wc_capture is -10% (growth consumes cash). CONTRACT LIABILITIES: LTA customer prepayments fell 1,983 (FY23) -> 1,584 -> 1,230 (FY25) -> 954 (Q2 2026); ~$1.1bn/yr of reported revenue is being 'released' from prepayments already sitting in the cash pile added at the bridge, so the remaining 954 is deducted in equity_bridge rather than assumed to keep growing; new LTA prepayments are drying up (additions ~770 FY25, ~120 H1-26). Horizon 10 years because the margin/capex/tax paths are still ramping at year 5. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical range 12-15x per the method; bear 12x, bull 16x). Controlled company (~81% Mubadala) and three consecutive years of ICFR material weaknesses are noted as governance risks and priced through the bear weight, not the WACC.

equity_bridge.item: Contract-liability unwind (LTA prepayments already collected, revenue still to be delivered)
equity_bridge.note: 954 of contract liabilities at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 6-K note: beginning 1,230, released 397 in H1-26). The cash is in the 3,303 liquid balance added to EV while the model recognises the revenue in FY26-FY28 with no matching cash; ~PV over ~2 years, rounded to 900.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle specialty-foundry growth anchored between equity_3yr_cagr (6.4%) and the FY2022-peak-to-FY2025 revenue path; equity_5yr_cagr is inflated by the Oct-2021 IPO proceeds
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 10.7% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 7.0% and from the -15.3% EPS 3yr CAGR: the equity series carries ~$1.5bn of 2021 IPO proceeds and the EPS series starts at the FY2022 cycle peak and ends after the FY2024 impairment. Neither is a usable growth anchor on its own.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs run FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), December year-ends. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - finance income): FY20 408, FY21 843, FY22 -667, FY23 22, FY24 710, FY25 650. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (FY2022 base negative in the capex supercycle year, 3,059 capex). The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR of 9.8% is half the reported-FCF CAGR of 19.6%: SBC went 1 -> 200 and finance income 3 -> 159 over the period, so a large share of reported FCF growth is stock-paid or is interest on the IPO cash rather than operating improvement. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 EPS -2.70).

base.growth_note: FY2026 +7% = H1-26 actual 3,420 + Q3 guide 1,885 + Q4 ~1,950 -> ~7,255; then mid-single-digit specialty-foundry growth (photonics/auto/comms up, smart mobile down) decelerating to 3%.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, pre-lease adjusted EBITDA margin: 32.2% H1-26 actual -> 35% mature, below the 36.6-36.9% FY22-24 peak-utilisation prints because acquired IP-business opex (~$300m/yr step-up) is now in the base.
base.capex_note: Net of government grant receipts (FY25 148). Gross program ~$1.6bn/yr over 10+ years; H1-26 capex 723 annualises to ~19-20% of revenue.
base.tax_note: FY25 cash taxes paid 19 on 911 pretax (2%). Ramp to 15% as US/German NOLs are consumed; 35% AMITC keeps US cash tax near zero through the Fab 8/9 build.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle recovery without a re-rating of the business model. Revenue reaches ~$7.25bn in FY2026 on the Q3 guide, then grows mid-single digits as Communications Infrastructure & Data Center (silicon photonics/SiGe, +47-62% YoY in H1-26) and Automotive content offset the structural decline in Smart Mobile Devices (39% of revenue, dual-sourcing and ASP pressure). Gross margin holds ~30% but the acquired MIPS/ARC/AMF/InfiniLink opex keeps pre-SBC EBITDA at 32.5-35%, below the 37% peak of the 2022-24 shortage era. Capex stays structurally heavy (~$1.3-1.5bn/yr net of CHIPS and NY State grants) as Fab 8/Fab 9 are built out, so owner FCF stays a single-digit share of revenue until the tax ramp and capex normalise. The ~$1bn contract-liability unwind is a cash headwind through FY2028 and no new LTA prepayment cycle is assumed. Cash tax stays low on NOLs and the 35% AMITC but ramps to 15%.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-adjacent photonics becomes a second core business. AMF makes GF the largest silicon-photonics pure-play; 400G/lambda, CPO and pluggables for AI data centres plus automotive design wins at Bosch and others push growth to 8-10% for three years. Utilisation returns to the high-80s/90s, GM passes 32% and pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 38%, the mix shifting toward single-sourced, higher-priced specialty nodes. Government funding (CHIPS DFA, $375m quantum award, $300m photonics LOI) keeps net capex at 15% of revenue and the AMITC holds cash tax at ~12%. Capital returns (dividend plus buyback) are funded from FCF without reducing the net cash pile. Terminal 3% growth, 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns again before the margin story completes. FY2027 flat and FY2028 -8% as smartphone weakness, Chinese mature-node overcapacity (SMIC/HuaHong ASP pressure) and further LTA renegotiations (customers pushing pricing and volume down, top-10 = 63% of volume, Customer A 16%) hit utilisation; pre-SBC EBITDA drops to 27% at the trough and recovers only to 31% because the higher-cost US/German/Singapore footprint cannot match Asian peers. The >$16bn fab program is not scaled back in step with revenue, so capex stays 17-20% of revenue and D&A rises. Export-control/tariff escalation adds friction on the Dresden/Singapore/China-facing business. Cash tax ramps to 18% as incentives expire. Mubadala continues selling down, capping the multiple. Terminal 2%, 12x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a high-fixed-cost cyclical that has already impaired $935m of capacity once this cycle, with top-10 customer concentration of 63% of volume, an active LTA renegotiation cycle, three consecutive years of ICFR material weaknesses and an 81% controlling shareholder that has sold stock into the market twice. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the photonics ramp, a full margin recovery to 38% AND no down-cycle over the horizon to all hold simultaneously. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value GF as what it is: a capital-intensive specialty foundry at mid-cycle, not at the utilisation peak the current quarter is climbing toward. Owner FCF charges SBC (~3% of revenue) and strips the finance income on the ~$3.3bn cash-and-securities pile that is added back at the bridge, and the model deducts the remaining LTA prepayments that were collected years ago and are now being recognised as revenue. The stock's valuation rests on non-IFRS adjusted FCF and adjusted EPS that exclude SBC and amortisation, and on gross margin expansion; the house basis is the cash an owner actually keeps after the fabs are funded. The gap between the house and street values is the price the market is paying for treating stock comp as non-cash, and the gap between the base and bull values is the price of the photonics/AI re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cyclicality: FY2022 peak revenue 8,108 vs FY2024 trough 6,750 with a $935m capacity impairment; a repeat down-cycle before the margin ramp completes is the bear case, weighted 25%
Capex intensity: >$16bn program over 10+ years is contingent on CHIPS Act / NY State milestone funding; a subsidy shortfall or clawback pushes net capex above the 16-19% of revenue modelled
Contract-liability unwind: ~$954m of prepaid LTA revenue still to be delivered with no cash; the model deducts it at the bridge, but faster LTA cancellations could turn into refunds or lower volumes
Customer concentration and LTA renegotiation: Customer A 16.4% and Customer C 13.9% of FY2025 wafer revenue; renegotiations lowered pricing/volumes in 2024-25 and more are expected in 2026
Smart Mobile Devices (39% of revenue) structural decline from dual-sourcing and memory-driven handset weakness; growth depends on photonics and automotive replacing it
Controlled company (~81% Mubadala) with consent rights and a history of secondary sales; ICFR material weaknesses in FY2023-FY2025 20-Fs not yet remediated
Export controls, tariffs (Jan-2026 25% tariff on advanced computing chips) and Chinese mature-node overcapacity pressure both volume and ASP in GF's nodes
Cash tax: the model ramps from 4% to 15%; loss of AMITC eligibility or faster NOL exhaustion raises cash tax sooner
Non-IFRS framing: the capital-return framework is set on non-IFRS adjusted FCF (pre-SBC); paying 50% of that out while SBC dilutes could push distributions above owner FCF
